comparator.name: Environmental Sciences
comparator.sourceNotes: The current 180-EC programme comprises a 120-EC common part, a 30-EC specialisation and 30 EC of free choice. The common part includes 105 EC of credited compulsory courses, a 3-EC mathematics/statistics choice and a 12-EC thesis. The broad Interdisciplinary Environmental Challenges specialisation is reconstructed with its required nexus course, two social-science options and two natural-science/technology selections in official order. Required non-credit safety modules are acknowledged but not encoded as credit-bearing components.

routeSelection.basis: The generic bachelor offers four current 30-EC specialisations. The interdisciplinary route most directly represents the programme’s published identity as a mix of natural, social and technological sciences, and is selected independently of UCR fit.

courses: New Issues in Contemporary Social Theory

core: Environmental systems linking atmosphere, water, soil, ecosystems and human activity
Scientific research, chemistry, mathematics, statistics, modelling and environmental evidence
Climate change, pollution, resource scarcity and sustainability transitions
adjacent: Environmental quality, ecology and resilient ecosystems
Environmental policy, economics, law and governance
Environmental technology, circular resources and sustainable energy
Geo-information, environmental data and spatial resource management
questions: How do human activities and natural processes cause environmental degradation?
How can environmental quality and ecosystem resilience be protected?
Which policy, technological and governance solutions enable sustainable transitions?

alternatives.label: Environmental systems, climate & sustainable solutions
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum integrates environmental systems, climate, soils, water, ecology, quantitative evidence, resource recovery, energy and governance.
alternatives.concept: The closest feasible UCR response to Environmental Sciences: an integrated natural-science programme linking Earth and ecosystem processes, climate, pollution, soils and water with data, observation, circular-resource solutions and sustainability governance.
progression: Environmental science, programming and mathematical foundations precede climate, observation, soils, water, numerical methods, biogeochemistry, remediation, research and advanced sustainability applications. Formal prerequisites and planned offerings pass; six 300-level courses are included.

alternatives.label: Environmental quality, ecosystems & resilience
alternatives.labelReason: This curriculum centres biodiversity, conservation, ecosystem processes, environmental quality, soils, water and ecological resilience while retaining climate and Earth-system foundations.
alternatives.concept: An environmental-quality and ecosystems direction connecting biodiversity, conservation and ecological processes with climate change, soil and water systems, contamination, remediation and resilience.
progression: Earth science, sustainability, ecology and life-science foundations precede conservation, climate, soils, aquifers, ecosystems, remediation, marine ecology, environmental justice and advanced research. Formal prerequisites and planned offerings pass; seven 300-level courses are included.
alternatives.distinctness: This route makes ecosystem condition, biodiversity, conservation and resilience the organising priority. Relative to the closest programme it replaces programming, mathematical and data-analysis courses with conservation, evolution, life-science and marine-ecology study; the pair differs by six courses and 45 EC in each direction.

alternatives.label: Environmental policy, governance & spatial sustainability
alternatives.labelReason: This curriculum combines environmental systems and spatial evidence with sociology, economics, politics, communication, participation and sustainability governance.
alternatives.concept: A policy-and-governance direction examining how institutions, economic choices, public participation and communication shape environmental change and sustainable spatial solutions.
progression: Environmental and social-science foundations precede policy, economics, spatial evidence, water governance, research, communication and advanced sustainability institutions. Formal prerequisites and planned offerings pass; nine 300-level courses are included.
alternatives.distinctness: This route makes institutions, economics, public participation and communication the organising priority. It differs from each science-led pathway by thirteen courses and 97.5 EC in each direction, replacing specialist environmental and ecological methods with a coherent social-science and governance sequence.

notes.text: WUR provides a prescribed environmental-sciences sequence in chemistry, pollution modelling, air quality, environmental technology, policy, economics and law, followed by a formal specialisation and thesis. UCR can combine substantial environmental science, ecology, climate, data, governance and sustainability study, but does not reproduce the same specialist laboratory, engineering or environmental-law sequence.

selection.assessment: The closest programme integrates environmental systems, climate, pollution, quantitative evidence and sustainable solutions. Environmental quality/ecosystem resilience and environmental policy/governance form two further evidenced, coherent and mechanically feasible directions. They are pairwise distinct by at least 45 EC, so production stops at the three-alternative maximum.
